gates.claim: extend(pi^2/6, rogersL)(x) = Re of the analytic Rogers L, at the SIX arguments Lean's `extended_sum` actually uses -- the level-7 orbit {1/(1-x), x, (x-1)/x} and its negatives, x the root of X^3-2X^2-X+1 in (1/2,1). These are the values the level-7 bridge (Route 32) needs, not a generic sample

the same identification across ALL THREE regimes of `extend`, 81 points each -- so the agreement is not an accident of the six arguments. On (0,1) the two agree identically (both are the series); the content is in x > 1 (inversion) and x < 0 (Landen)

d/dz [Li2(z) + Li2(z/(z-1)) + (1/2) log(1-z)^2] = 0 -- the analytic core of the Landen leg, and exactly what Lean's `hasDerivAt_landenCombo` proves. Sampled OFF the real axis as well, since the Lean statement is complex

the constant that zero derivative leaves undetermined is 0 -- i.e. Landen holds outright. Pinning it needs one special value, Li2(-1) = -pi^2/12 at the base point z = -1. AN EARLIER DRAFT OF THIS GATE SAID LEAN DID NOT HAVE IT; that is now false and is corrected: `QOU.Archimedean.LiTwo_neg_one` and `cLiTwo_neg_one` prove it, from `hasSum_alternating_zeta_two` -- a Mathlib gap filled here, since Mathlib has hasSum_zeta_two (pi^2/6) but no alternating analogue. What remains for Landen is only the connectedness step from zero derivative to the identity

WHAT LEAN STILL NEEDS, named per regime rather than left in prose. (0,1): nothing -- `cLiTwo_ofReal` already bridges the corpus's LiTwo to cLiTwo. x < 0 (Landen): the analytic core AND the base value Li2(-1) = -pi^2/12 are both proved; what remains is only the connectedness step from zero derivative to the identity. x > 1 (inversion): HARDER, and not attempted -- x > 1 lies ON cLiTwoExt's cut (notCut excludes real x >= 1), so it needs a BOUNDARY value from off the cut, not merely a constant of integration. Exactly one of the six arguments is in that regime, and it is unavoidable: it is w_1 = 2.24698
gates.landen_remaining: only the zero-derivative-to-identity connectedness step; the analytic core and the base value Li2(-1) = -pi^2/12 are both proved
gates.inversion_remaining: boundary values of Li2 on [1, inf) -- new analytic infrastructure

gates.claim: ADVERSARIAL on the Lean hypothesis: `hasDerivAt_landenCombo` requires 1 - z in slitPlane, and that is load-bearing, not decoration. At z = 3 the point 1 - z = -2 is a negative real, on log's cut, and log(1 - z/(z-1)) = -log(1-z) FAILS by exactly 2 pi i -- so the cancellation the theorem turns on would break. Dropping the hypothesis does not weaken the theorem, it falsifies it

verdict.measured: extend(pi^2/6, rogersL) = Re of the analytic Rogers L, to 1e-50, at the six arguments `extended_sum` uses and across all three regimes.
verdict.proved_this_round: the analytic core of the Landen leg -- the combination Li2(z) + Li2(z/(z-1)) + (1/2) log(1-z)^2 has zero derivative, with the branch condition isolated and shown load-bearing.
verdict.still_open: (a) for Landen, only the connectedness step -- its analytic core AND its base value Li2(-1) = -pi^2/12 are both now proved; (b) the INVERSION leg for x > 1, which needs boundary values of Li2 ON its cut -- new analytic infrastructure, and the sharper of the two. Exactly one of the six arguments needs it, w_1 = 2.24698, and it cannot be avoided.
